claim: ZOO Planckendael adult ticket is €34.50, children 3-11 €29.50, under 3 free, open 365 days a year
quote: Adults (18-25 and 60+): €34.50 Children (3-11): €29.50 Teenagers (12-17): €34.50 Young children (0-2): Free ... Open 365 days.

claim: Planckendael is a 42-hectare zoo near Mechelen housing hundreds of animal species across themed continental zones
quote: ZOO Planckendael in Mechelen is a zoo in Belgium that is 42 hectare in size ... hundreds of animal species from all five continents, including Asian and African lions, snow leopards, cheetahs, Indian rhinoceros, giraffes, zebras, Bonobo apes, kangaroos, koalas and red pandas.

claim: Technopolis Mechelen entry is €27 for ages 12-64, €22 for children 4-11, free under 4, €25.50 for 65+
Technopolis is open 09:30-17:00 normally and to 18:00 during Flemish school holidays, with shorter Wednesday hours (12:00-17:00) in term time
quote: Technopolis is usually open from 9:30 am to 5 pm, with adjusted hours on Wednesdays during the school term (12 noon to 5 pm). During the Flemish school holidays, the museum is open every day from 9:30 a.m. to 6:00 p.m.

claim: Fort van Duffel is a restored 1886-1888 railway fort at Mechelsebaan 249, with WWI exhibition, bat colonies, nature walk along the moat, and a brasserie staffed by young people with ASD
quote: The railway fort of Duffel was built in 1886-1888 from brick and concrete to protect the Antwerp-Brussels railway ... Nature walks along the outer moat with five observation points ... The site contains a brasserie operated by young people with autism spectrum disorders.

claim: Fort van Duffel is freely accessible, closed Mondays, open Tue-Sun 11:00 onwards with the exhibition included
quote: Access to the exhibition and surroundings is free. The fort is closed Mondays; Tuesday to Friday: 11:00-21:00, Saturday: 11:00-22:00, Sunday: 11:00-21:00.

claim: Fort 5 in Edegem plus adjacent Hof ter Linden form a ~90-hectare green zone with 3 km nature path, treehouse, playground and a play forest 'Dikke Bertha', open daily 06:45-21:00
quote: Fort 5 forms together with Hof Ter Linden one large green area of almost 90 hectares ... Fort 5 is open daily year-round from 6:45 to 21:00 ... a play forest called 'Dikke Bertha' where children can build camps, slide down a slide and climb in a tree house.

claim: Museum Fort Liezele in Puurs-Sint-Amands is open daily 10:00-17:00 except Tuesdays, visit takes ~2 hours with included quadrilingual audio guide
quote: The fort is open daily from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. except Tuesdays ... A visit takes about two hours and a quadrilingual audio guide is included.

claim: Fort van Walem is not freely accessible (structurally unsafe) but Natuurpunt runs guided visits on the last Sunday of the month April-September; an outer-moat walking path is always open
quote: Het fort is niet vrij toegankelijk omdat het bouwvallig is ... Iedere laatste zondag van maand (april tot september), kan het fort bezocht worden onder begeleiding van een gids ... Rond de gracht ligt ook een wandelpad dat altijd toegankelijk is.

claim: Fort van Koningshooikt (1907-1908) near Lier is a recreation/events venue not open to individuals but cycling and walking around the moat is possible and links to the broader fort ring
quote: The Fortress of Koningshooikt was built in 1907-1908 ... it is home to several associations, and you can walk and cycle around the canal ... Cyclists can discover the fort together with Fort van Duffel, Fort van Lier, Fort van Koningshooikt, Fort van Sint-Katelijne-Waver, and Fort van Walem via the route 'Langs Nete en groentestreek'.

claim: Vrijbroekpark in Mechelen is a 75-hectare provincial domain with three marked walks (Tree 1.5 km, Herb 1.5 km, Rose 2.5 km), one of Europe's finest rose collections, dahlia garden and a playground, free access sunrise-sunset
quote: Vrijbroekpark is a green area of 75 hectares on the edge of the city of Mechelen ... three marked walking routes: the Tree Walk (1.5 km), the Herb Walk (1.5 km) and the Rose Walk (2.5 km) ... one of the most beautiful rose collections in Europe

claim: Duffel's nature areas include the Mosterdpot/Goorbosbeek visitor centre, the 4.5-ha Babbelbeekse Beemden with wooden boardwalk, and a ~20-ha Oude Spoorwegberm tied into the Rivierenland walking network
quote: Babbelbeekse Beemden: This is a 4.5 hectare nature area ... A wooden boardwalk was installed in summer 2018 ... Oude Spoorwegberm ... is a nature area of almost 20 hectares. This section is part of the Rivierenland walking node network.

claim: The Duffel walking loop 'Langs Mosterdpot en Goorbosbeek' is 7.5 km through play-nature, Mouriaubos, a barefoot path and the Goorbosbeek valley
quote: The Rivierenland walking area includes the new Duffel walking trail 'Langs Mosterdpot en Goorbosbeek,' a 7.5 km loop that leads you through the Mosterdpot play nature, Mouriaubos, a barefoot path, and the beautiful Goorbosbeek valley.

claim: Hof van Ringen in Lier is an 1849 neoclassical castle on the Nete in a 24-hectare park, now owned by fashion designer Dries Van Noten and viewable from the surrounding Pallieter walking routes
quote: The castle was built in 1849 in Neoclassical style with Palladian features on the banks of the Nete river. The castle is situated in a 24-hectare domain with ponds ... The current owner and resident of Hof van Ringen is Belgian fashion designer Dries Van Noten.

claim: The F1 fietssnelweg follows the Antwerp-Mechelen railway through Duffel (via Berchem, Mortsel, Hove, Kontich, Sint-Katelijne-Waver, Nekkerspoel), is fully ridable and signposted, part of a 46 km Antwerp-Brussels axis
quote: The route follows the railroad line from Antwerp to Mechelen, passing via Berchem, Mortsel Oude-God, Hove, Kontich, Duffel, Sint-Katelijne-Waver and Mechelen-Nekkerspoel, and the entire route is rideable and signposted.

claim: Fietsknooppunten routes from Lier follow the Nete through Duffel and onward toward the Kempen, using Belgium's numbered-node cycle network
quote: Routes quickly arrive in Duffel on the Nete, and then cycle along the Nete to Lier.

claim: Blue-bike rentals are available at Mechelen station, Mechelen Nekkerspoel and Veemarkt for €2.50/day (city subsidy) with €12/year membership
quote: In Mechelen, you can rent a Blue-bike for just €2.50 per day instead of €3.50, as the city of Mechelen contributes €1, and you pay €12 per year for membership.

claim: Sportoase Mechelen swimming pool is open weekdays 07:00-22:00 and weekends/holidays 08:00-18:00, with a separate recreation/wellness zone and slide complex
quote: Monday to Friday: 07:00-22:00 Saturday-Sunday and holidays: 08:00-18:00
